summary.name: Institutional repository
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article describing institutional repositories: university-run digital archives that collect, preserve and share an institution's research output and other digital materials.
use_cases: Providing open access to published articles
Preserving grey literature such as working papers and technical reports
summary.what_it_does: The article defines an institutional repository as a set of university services for managing and disseminating digital materials created by the institution and its members. It covers typical contents such as preprints, postprints, datasets, theses and course notes. It explains the functions of such repositories, including preservation, open access self-archiving, and research assessment. It also describes how repositories interoperate via OAI-PMH and how aggregators such as BASE, CORE and Unpaywall index their content. The page does not describe a specific software product, though it mentions DSpace as supporting OAI-PMH.
notable: Defined through Clifford Lynch's 2003 description of university repository services
Covers the green open access (self-archiving) route
Explains OAI-PMH interoperability and aggregators such as BASE, CORE and Unpaywall
Lists related items such as CRIS, the Registry of Open Access Repositories and ResCarta Toolkit
caveats: Describes a concept rather than a downloadable tool; no software product is documented on the page
Page notes most university outputs are not effectively accessed and shared
Survey cited notes 72% of respondents host their repository with a third party
